cues.en: Well, it's a real pleasure
cues.zh: 真的非常荣幸。

cues.en: to be here and to have a chance just to meet with you and talk about some of the problems that we're facing. Now, some of these problems are local, some are national, some are global,
cues.zh: 很高兴能来到这里，有机会与大家见面，聊聊我们正面临的一些问题。这些问题中，有些是本地性的，有些是全国性的，有些是全球性的，

cues.en: but they're all tied together.
cues.zh: 但它们都紧密相连。

cues.en: They're tied together with arithmetic, and the arithmetic isn't very difficult.
cues.zh: 它们通过算术联系在一起，而且这些算术并不难。

cues.en: And what I hope to do is I hope to be able to convince you
cues.zh: 而我想要做的，就是希望能说服各位

cues.en: that the greatest shortcoming of the human race is our inability
cues.zh: 人类最大的缺点就是我们无法……

cues.en: to understand the exponential
cues.zh: 要理解指数级增长

cues.en: function.
cues.zh: 函数。

cues.en: So you say, well, what's the exponential function?
cues.zh: 于是你说，嗯，指数函数是什么呢？

cues.en: This is a mathematical function that you would write down if you're going to describe the size of anything that was growing steadily. If you had something growing 5% per year, you'd write the exponential function to show how large that growing quantity was year after year.
cues.zh: 这是一个数学函数，如果你想描述任何稳定增长的东西的大小，就会用到它。比如某样东西每年增长 5%，你就会写出这个指数函数，来表示这个增长的量年复一年有多大。

cues.en: And so we're talking about a situation
cues.zh: 所以我们在讨论这样一种情况

cues.en: where the time that's required for the growing quantity
cues.zh: 其中，随着数量不断增长所需花费的时间

cues.en: to increase by a fixed fraction is a constant. 5% per year, the 5% is a fixed fraction. The per year is a fixed length of time. Now, that's what we want to talk about. It's ordinary steady growth.
cues.zh: 按固定比例增长就是恒定增长。每年 5%，这 5% 是固定比例。“每年”是固定长度的时间。现在，这就是我们要讨论的内容。这是普通的稳定增长。

cues.en: Well, if it takes a fixed length of time to grow 5%,
cues.zh: 嗯，如果增长5%需要一段固定的时间，

cues.en: it follows it takes a longer fixed length of time to grow 100%.
cues.zh: 由此可见，要增长到 100% 需要更长的固定时间。

cues.en: Now, that longer time is called a doubling time.
cues.zh: 而这个更长的时间叫作翻倍时间。

cues.en: We need to know how you calculate the doubling time, and it's easy. You just take the number 70,
cues.zh: 我们需要知道怎么计算翻倍时间，其实很简单。你只需取数字 70，

cues.en: divide it by the percent growth per unit time, and that gives you the doubling time. So, our example of 5% per year, you divide the five into 70, you find that growing quantity will double in size every fourteen years.
cues.zh: 用每单位时间的增长百分比去除它，就得到翻倍时间。比如每年增长 5% 的例子，拿 70 除以 5，你会发现这个增长量每 14 年翻一番。

cues.en: Well, you might ask, where did the 70 come from? The answer is it's approximately 100
cues.zh: 你可能会问，这个 70 是从哪来的？答案是，它大约是 100。

cues.en: multiplied by the natural logarithm of two. If you wanted the time to triple, you'd use the natural logarithm of three, so it's all very logical.
cues.zh: 乘以二的自然对数。如果你想让时间变成三倍，那就用三的自然对数，所以说这一切都非常合乎逻辑。

cues.en: But you don't have to remember where it came from if you'll just remember 70.
cues.zh: 但你只要记住 70，就不用记它从哪儿来的了。

cues.en: Now, I wish we could get every person to make this mental calculation
cues.zh: 现在，我希望每个人都能做这个心算。

cues.en: every time we see a percent growth rate of anything in a news story.
cues.zh: 每当我们在新闻报道中看到某个指标以百分比表示的增长率时。

cues.en: For example, if you saw a story that said things have been growing 7% per year for several recent years, you wouldn't bat an eyelash. But when you see a headline that says crime has doubled in a decade, you say, my heavens, what's happening?
cues.zh: 比如说，如果你看到一则新闻报道说，近几年某样东西一直以每年 7% 的速度增长，你不会觉得有什么稀奇。但当你看到一条标题说十年间犯罪率翻了一倍，你就会惊叹：天哪，这是怎么了？

cues.en: What is happening?
cues.zh: 发生了什么？

cues.en: growth per year.
cues.zh: 每年增长。

cues.en: Divide the seven into 70, the doubling time is ten years. But notice, if you're going to write a headline, you never write crime growing 7%
cues.zh: 把 70 除以 7，翻倍时间就是 10 年。但注意，如果你要写标题，绝不会写“犯罪率增长 7%”。

cues.en: per year because most people wouldn't know what it really means.
cues.zh: 每年，因为大多数人并不知道它真正的含义。

cues.en: Now, do you know what 7% really means? Let's take another example from Colorado. The cost of an all day lift ticket to ski at Vail has
cues.zh: 现在，你知道 7% 到底意味着什么吗？我们再看一个来自科罗拉多州的例子。在 Vail 滑雪，一张全天缆车票的价格已经

cues.en: been growing about 7%
cues.zh: 增长了约 7%

cues.en: per year ever since Vail first opened in 1963,
cues.zh: 自 1963 年 Vail 首次开放以来，每年，

cues.en: and at that time you paid $5
cues.zh: 当时你付了5美元。

cues.en: for an all day lift ticket.
cues.zh: 全天缆车票。

cues.en: Now, what's the doubling time for 7% growth?
cues.zh: 那么，7% 增长的倍增时间是多少呢？

cues.en: Ten years. So what was the cost ten years later in 1973?
cues.zh: 十年。那么，十年后的 1973 年，代价是什么？

cues.en: Ten years later in 1983?
cues.zh: 十年后，1983年？

cues.en: Ten years later in 1993?
cues.zh: 十年后的 1993 年？

cues.en: And what do we have to look forward to?
cues.zh: 那么，我们又能期待些什么呢？

cues.en: Now this is what 7%
cues.zh: 现在这就是7%的样子。

cues.en: means.
cues.zh: 意味着。

cues.en: Most people don't have a clue.
cues.zh: 大多数人都毫无头绪。

cues.en: Let's look at a generic graph of something that's growing steadily.
cues.zh: 我们来看一个表示稳步增长事物的通用图表。

cues.en: After one doubling time, the growing quantity is up to twice its initial size. Two doubling times, it's up to four times its initial size.
cues.zh: 经过一个倍增周期，增长的数量会达到初始规模的两倍。经过两个倍增周期，就会达到初始规模的四倍。

cues.en: Then it goes to eight, 16, 32, 64,

cues.zh: 请提供需要翻译的英文演讲字幕内容。

cues.en: two fifty six, five twelve.
cues.zh: 二百五十六，五百一十二。

cues.en: In just 10 doubling times, it's a thousand times larger than when it started. And you can see, if you tried to make a graph of that on ordinary graph paper, the graph will go right through the ceiling.
cues.zh: 只需经历 10 次翻倍，它的大小就会变成起初的 1000 倍。你可以想象，如果用普通方格纸来画这个图，曲线会一直冲出纸面。

cues.en: Now let me give you an example to show the enormous numbers you get with just a modest number of doublings.
cues.zh: 现在我举个例子，看看只要翻倍几次，数字就会变得多么惊人。

cues.en: Legend has it that the game of chess was invented by a mathematician to work for a king. The king was very pleased. He said, I want to reward you. And the mathematician said, my needs are modest.
cues.zh: 传说国际象棋是一位数学家为一位国王发明的。国王非常高兴，他说：我要奖赏你。数学家说：我的要求不高。

cues.en: Please take my new chessboard, and on the first square, place one grain of wheat. On the next square, double a one to make two. On the next square, double a two to make four. Just keep doubling till you've doubled for every square. That will be an adequate payment.
cues.zh: 请用我的新棋盘：第一格放一粒麦子。下一格翻一倍，放两粒；再下一格把两粒翻倍，放四粒。就这样一直翻倍，直到每个格子都放好麦粒。这样付给我的报酬就够了。

cues.en: Well, we can guess the king thought this foolish man.
cues.zh: 我们可以猜到，国王认为这个人很愚蠢。

cues.en: I was ready to give him a real reward. All he asked for is just a few grains of wheat.
cues.zh: 我本打算给他一份真正的赏赐，而他想要的却只是几粒麦子。

cues.en: Well, let's see what's involved in this. We note there are eight grains on the fourth square.
cues.zh: 好，我们来看看这涉及什么。我们注意到第四个格子上有八粒谷物。

cues.en: Now, I can get this number eight by multiplying three twos together. It's two times two times two. It's one two less than the number of the square. Now, that follows in each case. So, on the last square, I'd find the number of grains by multiplying 63
cues.zh: 现在，我可以通过把三个 2 相乘得到这个数字 8。也就是 2 乘 2 乘 2。它比该棋格的编号少一个 2。现在，每种情况都遵循这一点。所以，在最后一个棋格上，我会通过把 63 个 2 相乘来得到麦粒数量。

cues.en: twos together.
cues.zh: 两个两个放在一起。

cues.en: Now, let's look at the way the totals build up. When we have one grain on the first square, the total on the board is one. We add two grains, that makes a total three. We put on four grains, now the total is seven.
cues.zh: 现在来看看总数是如何累加的。第一个格子上放 1 粒麦子时，棋盘上的总数是 1。再加 2 粒，总数变成 3。放 4 粒上去，现在总数是 7。

cues.en: Seven is a grain less than eight, it's a grain less than three twos multiplied together.
cues.zh: 七比八少一粒，它也比三个二相乘少一粒。

cues.en: 15 is a grain less than four twos multiplied together.
cues.zh: 15 是一个小于四个 2 相乘结果的整数。

cues.en: Continues in each case. When we're done, the total number of grains will be one grain less than the number I get multiplying 64
cues.zh: 每种情况都继续下去。完成后，谷粒总数将比我把 64 相乘得到的数少一粒。

cues.en: twos together. And my question is, how much wheat is that?
cues.zh: 把那些二乘在一起。我的问题是，那到底得有多少麦子？

cues.en: You know, would that be a nice pile here in the studio?
cues.zh: 你想啊，那一堆东西放在演播室里，是不是挺不错的？

cues.en: Would it fill the building?
cues.zh: 能装满这栋楼吗？

cues.en: Would it cover the county to adapt the two meters? How much wheat are we talking about?
cues.zh: 改装这两个仪表能覆盖全县吗？我们说的是多少小麦？

cues.en: The answer is it's roughly
cues.zh: 答案是，它大致是

cues.en: times the 1990
cues.zh: 是 1990 年的多少倍

cues.en: worldwide harvest of wheat.
cues.zh: 全球小麦收成。

cues.en: Now, that could be more wheat than humans have harvested in the entire history of the earth. You say, how did you get such a big number? Well, it was simple. We just started with one grain, but we let the number grow steadily till it had doubled a mere 63 times.
cues.zh: 这可能比人类在地球历史上收获的小麦总量还要多。你可能会问，这么大的数字是怎么算出来的？很简单。我们从一粒麦子开始，让数量持续增长，只翻了 63 次。

cues.en: There's something else that's very important. The growth in any doubling time is greater than the total of all of the preceding growth.
cues.zh: 还有一点非常重要。每次翻倍所增加的数量，都大于此前所有增长量的总和。

cues.en: For example, when we put eight grains on the fourth square, the eight is larger than the total of seven that were already there. When we put 32 grains on the sixth square, the 32 is larger than the total of 31 that were already there. Every time the growing quantity doubles, it takes more than all that you'd used in all of the preceding growth.
cues.zh: 比如，在第四个方格上放八粒麦子时，八就大于那里原先已有的七粒总数。在第六个方格上放 32 粒麦子时，32 就大于那里原先已有的 31 粒总数。每当数量翻倍时，新增的数量就超过此前所有增长量的总和。

cues.en: Now, let's translate that into the energy crisis. Here's an ad from the year 1975,
cues.zh: 现在，我们把这个道理应用到能源危机上。这是一则 1975 年的广告，

cues.en: and it asked the question,
cues.zh: 它提出了这样一个问题：

cues.en: could America run out of electricity?
cues.zh: 美国会不会用光电力？

cues.en: America depends on electricity. Our need for electricity actually doubles every ten or twelve years.
cues.zh: 美国依赖电力。我们对电力的需求实际上每十到十二年就会翻倍。

cues.en: That's an accurate reflection of a very long history of steady growth of the electric industry in this country, growth at a rate of around 7%
cues.zh: 这准确反映了美国电力行业长期稳定增长的历史，增长率大约是 7%

cues.en: per year, which goes with doubling every ten years. Now, with all that history of growth, expected the growth would just go on forever.
cues.zh: 每年，这意味着每十年翻一倍。鉴于这种持续增长的历史，人们预计这种增长会永远持续下去。

cues.en: Fortunately, stopped.
cues.zh: 幸好，它停止了。

cues.en: Not because anyone understood the arithmetic, it stopped for other reasons. But let's ask, what if?
cues.zh: 不是因为有人理解了其中的算术，而是因为其他原因停止了。但我们来问问，假如呢？

cues.en: Suppose the growth had continued,
cues.zh: 假设这种增长持续下去，

cues.en: then we would see here the thing that we just saw on the chessboard.
cues.zh: 那么我们就会看到刚才在棋盘上看到的情况。

cues.en: In the ten years following the appearance of this ad, in that decade,
cues.zh: 在这则广告出现后的十年里，也就是那十年中，

cues.en: the amount of electrical energy that we would have consumed in this country would have been greater than the total of all of the electrical
cues.zh: 我们这个国家消耗的电能总量将会超过此前电力行业在这个国家稳定增长的整个历史中所消耗的全部电能

cues.en: we had ever consumed in the entire preceding history
cues.zh: 的总和

cues.en: of the steady growth of that industry in this country.
cues.zh: 这个国家该行业的稳步发展。

cues.en: Now, did you realize
cues.zh: 你有没有意识到，

cues.en: that anything is completely acceptable? A 7% growth per year could give such an incredible consequence that in just ten years you'd use more than the total of all that have been used in all of preceding history.
cues.zh: 一个完全可以接受的情况？每年 7% 的增长，竟然会造成如此惊人的后果：仅仅十年里，你消耗的电量就会超过此前整个历史上消耗量的总和。

cues.en: Well, that's exactly what President Carter was referring to in his famous speech on energy.
cues.zh: 这正是 Carter 总统在那次著名的能源演讲中所说的。

cues.en: One of his statements was this. He said, and in each of those decades,
cues.zh: 他说过这样一句话。在每一个这样的十年里，

cues.en: more oil was consumed than in all of mankind's previous history.
cues.zh: 消耗的石油都超过了人类此前整个历史所消耗的石油总量。

cues.en: Now, by itself, that's a stunning statement.
cues.zh: 单独听起来，这是一句令人震撼的话。

cues.en: Now you can understand it. The President was telling us a simple consequence of the arithmetic
cues.zh: 现在你能理解了。总统是在告诉我们，每年 7%

cues.en: of 7%
cues.zh: 增长率

cues.en: growth each year in world oil consumption, and that was the historic figure up until the 1970s.
cues.zh: 所带来的一个简单算术结果：世界石油消费量每年增长 7%，而这正是截至 20 世纪 70 年代之前的历史数据。

cues.en: Now, there's another beautiful consequence of this arithmetic.
cues.zh: 现在，这种算术还有另一个精彩的结果。

cues.en: If you take seventy years as a period of time and note that that's roughly one human lifetime,
cues.zh: 如果以七十年为一个时间段，并注意到这大约是一个人的寿命，

cues.en: then any percent growth continued steadily for seventy years gives you an overall increase by a factor that's very easy to calculate.
cues.zh: 然后，只要百分比增长持续七十年，最终的增长倍数就很容易算出来。

cues.en: For example, 4% per year,
cues.zh: 例如，每年 4%，

cues.en: you find the factor by multiplying four twos together, it's a factor of 16.
cues.zh: 你把四个 2 相乘就得到这个因数，它是 16 的一个因数。

cues.en: Now, a few years ago, one of the newspapers here in Boulder quizzed the nine members of the Boulder City Council and asked them, What rate of growth of Boulder's population do you think it would be good to have in the coming years? Now the nine members of the Boulder City Council gave answers ranging from a low of 1% per year. Now that happens to match the present rate of growth of the population of The United States. We are not at zero population growth. Right now, the number of Americans is increasing by more than 3,000,000
cues.zh: 几年前，博尔德当地的一家报纸调查了博尔德市议会的九位成员，问他们：你认为未来几年博尔德人口的增长率保持在多少比较合适？九位成员给出的答案从每年最低 1% 不等。这个数字恰好与当下美国人口的增长率相吻合。我们目前并不处于人口零增长状态。就在此刻，美国人口正以每年超过 300 万的速度增长。

cues.en: people every year.
cues.zh: 每年都有人。

cues.en: No member of the city council said Boulders should grow less rapidly than The United States is growing.
cues.zh: 市议会没有人说，Boulders 的发展速度应该低于美国。

cues.en: Now the highest answer any council member gave was 5%
cues.zh: 委员会成员给出的最高答案也只有 5%。

cues.en: per year.
cues.zh: 每年。

cues.en: Well, you know, felt compelled. I had to write them a letter and say, Did you know
cues.zh: 嗯，你知道，我觉得非得这么做。我得给他们写封信，说：你知道吗

cues.en: that 5% growth
cues.zh: 那 5% 的增长

cues.en: for just seventy years? I can remember when seventy years used to seem like an awful long time. It doesn't seem so long now.
cues.zh: 才七十年吗？我记得以前七十年似乎漫长得不得了。现在似乎没那么长了。

cues.en: Well, means Boulder's population would increase by a factor of 32.
cues.zh: 也就是说，Boulder 的人口会变成原来的 32 倍。

cues.en: That is where today we have one overloaded sewer treatment plant in seventy years. We'd need 32 overloaded sewer treatment plants.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么如今七十年才会有一座超负荷运转的污水处理厂，而我们将需要 32 座超负荷运转的污水处理厂。

cues.en: Now, did you realize that anything as completely all American as 5% growth per year could give such an incredible consequence
cues.zh: 你有没有意识到，像每年5%增长这种再典型不过的美国式指标，竟能带来如此惊人的结果

cues.en: in such a modest period of time?
cues.zh: 这么短的时间里？

cues.en: Our City Council people had zero
cues.zh: 我们市议会的人完全没有】【。

cues.en: understanding
cues.zh: 理解

cues.en: of this very simple arithmetic.
cues.zh: 这个非常简单的算术。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: a few years ago I had a class of non science students who were interested in problems of science and society.
cues.zh: 几年前，我教过一个非理科生班级，他们对科学与社会的问题很感兴趣。

cues.en: We spent a good deal of time learning to use semi logarithmic
cues.zh: 我们花了大量时间学习使用半对数

cues.en: graph paper.
cues.zh: 坐标纸。

cues.en: It's printed in such a way that these equal intervals along the vertical scale each represent an increase by a factor of 10.
cues.zh: 它的打印方式是，纵轴上这些相等的区间各自代表增长 10 倍。

cues.en: So, you go from a thousand to 10,000 to a 100,000
and the reason you use this special paper is that on this paper a straight line represents steady growth.
cues.zh: 之所以用这种特殊的纸，是因为在这种纸上，直线代表稳定增长。

cues.en: We worked a lot of examples. I said to the students, let's talk about inflation. Let's talk about 7%
cues.zh: 我们做了很多例子。我对学生们说，我们来聊聊通货膨胀吧，聊聊 7%

cues.en: per year. It wasn't this high when we did this. It's been higher since then, and fortunately, it's lower now. And I said to the students, As I can say to you, you have roughly sixty years life expectancy ahead of you. Let's see what some common things will cost if we have sixty years of 7% annual inflation.
cues.zh: 每年。我们做这个的时候还没这么高。之后更高过，好在现在低了。我对学生说，正如我也可以对你们说的，你们前面大约还有六十年的预期寿命。如果每年7%的通胀持续六十年，来看看一些常见东西会花多少钱。

cues.en: Well, the students found that a 55¢
cues.zh: 学生们发现，55美分的

cues.zh: 现在，那幅漫画里有一个非常深刻的教训。这个教训就是，零人口增长将会发生。

cues.zh: 现在，我们可以争论自己是喜欢还是不喜欢零人口增长。

cues.en: It's going to happen whether we debate it or not, whether we like it or not. It's absolutely certain people could not live at that density on the dry land surface of the earth. Therefore, today's high birth rates will drop.
cues.zh: 无论我们争论与否，无论我们喜欢与否，它都会发生。人类绝对不可能以那种密度生活在地球陆地表面。因此，今天的高出生率将会下降。

cues.en: So, maybe you're wondering what sort of options are available if we wanted to address the problem.

cues.en: Just look at the list. Everything in the list is as sacred as motherhood.
cues.zh: 看看这份清单。清单上的每一项都像母性一样神圣。

cues.en: There's immigration,
cues.zh: 有移民，

cues.en: medicine, public health, sanitation.
cues.zh: 医疗、公共卫生、环境卫生。

cues.en: These are all devoted to the humane goals of lowering the death rate. And that's very important to me if it's my death they're lowering.
cues.zh: 这些都致力于降低死亡率的人道目标。如果被降低的是我的死亡风险，那对我非常重要。

cues.en: But then I have to realize that anything that just lowers the death rate makes the population problem worse.
cues.zh: 但我必须意识到，任何仅仅降低死亡率的事情，都会让人口问题更糟。

cues.en: There's peace,
cues.zh: 有和平，

cues.en: law and order.
cues.zh: 法律与秩序。

cues.en: Scientific agriculture has lowered the death rate due to famine. That just makes the population problem worse.
cues.zh: 科学农业降低了饥荒造成的死亡率。这只会让人口问题更糟。

cues.en: The 55 miles per hour speed limit saved thousands of lives.
cues.zh: 每小时55英里的限速拯救了数千条生命。

cues.en: Makes the population problem worse. Clean air makes it worse.
cues.zh: 让人口问题更糟。清洁空气也让问题更糟。

cues.en: Now, in this column are some of the things we should encourage if we want to lower the rate of growth of population and in so doing help solve the population problem.
cues.zh: 现在，这一栏里是一些事情；如果我们想降低人口增长率、从而帮助解决人口问题，就该鼓励这些事情。

cues.zh: 停止移民，

cues.zh: 好，我们看看瓶子里最后几分钟。中午十二点，满了。一分钟前，半满。两分钟前，四分之一满。然后八分之一、十六分之一。

cues.zh: 我问你们，在十二点前五分钟，瓶子只装了3%，还有97%

cues.en: open space just yearning for development,
cues.zh: 是开放空间，正渴望开发，

cues.en: how many of you would realize there was a problem?
cues.zh: 你们有多少人会意识到有问题？

cues.en: Now, in the ongoing controversy over growth in Boulder, someone wrote to the newspaper some years ago and said, 'Look, there isn't any problem with population growth in Boulder because,' the writer said, we have 15
cues.zh: 关于 Boulder 的发展争议持续不断，几年前有人给报纸写信说：“看，Boulder 的人口增长根本不算问题，因为，”作者写道，“我们拥有的未开发空间是已开发面积的 15

cues.en: times as much open space as we've already used. So let me ask you what time was it in Boulder when the open space was 15 times the amount of space we'd already used?
cues.zh: 倍。那么请问，当未开发空间还是已用面积的 15 倍时，Boulder 处在哪个时间点？

cues.en: The answer is it was four minutes before twelve in Boulder Valley.
cues.zh: 答案是，在 Boulder 谷地，当时相当于 11 点 56 分。

cues.en: Well, suppose that at two minutes before twelve, some of the bacteria realize that they're running out of space, so they launch a great search for new bottles.
cues.zh: 那么，假设在 11 点 58 分，有些细菌意识到空间快不够用了，于是开始大规模搜寻新的瓶子。

cues.en: And they search offshore
cues.zh: 它们在近海搜寻，

cues.en: on the outer continental shelf, in the overthrust belt, and in the Arctic,
cues.zh: 在外大陆架、在逆冲断裂带、在北极搜寻，

cues.en: and they find three new bottles. Now, that is a colossal discovery.
cues.zh: 结果找到了三个新瓶子。这可真是一项惊天大发现。

cues.en: That discovery is three times the amount of resource they ever knew about before. They now have four bottles.
cues.zh: 这个发现意味着资源量达到了它们已知储量的三倍。现在它们拥有四个瓶子了。

cues.en: Before the discovery, there was only one.
cues.zh: 而在发现之前，只有一个。

cues.en: Now surely,
cues.zh: 那么想必，

cues.en: this will give them a sustainable society.
cues.zh: 这下能换来一个可持续发展的社会了吧。

cues.en: Won't it?
cues.zh: 难道不是吗？

cues.en: Well, you know what the third question is. How long can the growth continue as a result of this magnificent
cues.zh: 大家自然知道第三个问题是什么了。由于这项宏伟的

cues.en: discovery?
cues.zh: 发现，增长还能持续多久？

cues.en: Well, let's look at the score. At twelve noon, one bottle is filled. There are three to go. At 12:01,
cues.zh: 我们来看看账。中午 12 点整，第一个瓶子满了，还剩三个。12 点 01 分，

cues.en: two bottles are filled. There are two to go. And at 12:02,
cues.zh: 两个瓶子满了，还剩两个。到了 12 点 02 分，

cues.en: all four are filled. And that's the end of the line.
cues.zh: 四个瓶子全满了。一切到此为止。

cues.en: Now, you don't need any more arithmetic than this to evaluate the absolutely
cues.zh: 只要具备这点算术常识，就足以看清那些完全

cues.en: contradictory
cues.zh: 自相矛盾的

cues.en: statements we've all heard and read from experts
cues.zh: 言论了——我们常听到专家们

cues.en: who tell us in one breath we can go on, increasing our rates of consumption of fossil fuels. In the next breath, they say, but don't worry. We'll always be able to make the discoveries of new resources that we need to meet the requirements of that growth.
cues.zh: 前脚跟我们说，大可继续提高化石燃料的消耗速度；后脚又说，别担心，我们总能发现新资源，满足这种增长的需求。

cues.en: Well, some years ago in Washington, our energy secretary observed
cues.zh: 几年前在华盛顿，我们的能源部长指出，

cues.en: that in the energy crisis,
cues.zh: 在这场能源危机中，

cues.en: we have a classic case
cues.zh: 我们面对的是一个典型案例——

cues.en: of exponential growth
cues.zh: 即指数级增长

cues.en: against a finite source.
cues.zh: 撞上了有限的资源。

cues.en: So, let's look at some of these finite sources. From the work of the late Doctor. M. King Hubbard, We have here his semi logarithmic plot of world oil production.
cues.zh: 那我们就来看看其中一些有限资源。根据已故 M. King Hubbard 博士的研究成果，这里有一张他绘制的全球石油产量半对数图。

cues.en: The line's been approximately straight for over a hundred years, clear up here to the year 1970.
cues.zh: 有一百多年来，这条曲线几乎就是一条直线，一直延伸到 1970 年。

cues.en: Average growth rate, very close to 7%
cues.zh: 年均增长率非常接近 7%

cues.en: per year. So it's logical to ask, well, how much longer could that 7%
cues.zh: 每年。所以很自然会问：这种 7% 的增长

cues.en: continue?
cues.zh: 还能持续多久？

cues.en: Well, that's answered by the numbers in this table.
cues.zh: 这张表里的数字给出了答案。

cues.en: In the top line, the numbers tell us that in the year 1973,
cues.zh: 第一行的数据告诉我们，在 1973 年，

cues.en: world oil production was 20,000,000,000
cues.zh: 全球石油年产量是 200 亿

cues.en: barrels. The total production in all of history, including that 20, was 300,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 桶。人类有史以来的总开采量（算上这 200 亿）是 3000 亿桶。

cues.en: The remaining reserves,
cues.zh: 而剩余的储量，
是 1.7 万亿桶。

cues.en: Now those are data.
cues.zh: 这些都是实际数据。

cues.en: The rest of this table is just calculated out. Assume that the historic 7%
cues.zh: 这个表格的其余部分只是推算出来的。假设历史上 7% 的

cues.en: growth continued steadily each year following 1973
cues.zh: 增长率在 1973 年之后每年稳步持续，

cues.en: exactly as it had been for the preceding one hundred years.
cues.zh: 完全就像过去一百年间那样。

cues.en: Now, in fact, the growth stopped.
cues.zh: 事实上，这种增长停止了。

cues.en: Not because of the arithmetic, it stopped because OPEC raised their oil prices. So we're asking, what if?
cues.zh: 不是因为数学算术，而是因为 OPEC 提高了石油价格。所以我们要问，如果当时继续增长会怎样？

cues.en: Suppose the growth had continued.
cues.zh: 假设增长一直持续下去。

cues.en: Let's go back to the year 1981.
cues.zh: 我们回到 1981 年。

cues.en: on the 7% curve, the total usage in all of history would add up to 500,000,000,000
cues.zh: 按照 7% 的增长曲线，人类历史上的总消耗量将达到 5000 亿

cues.en: barrels, the remaining reserves 1,500,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 桶，剩余储量为 15000 亿桶。

cues.en: The reserves at that point are three times the total of all that have been used in all of history.
cues.zh: 到那时，储量是整个人类历史上消耗总量的三倍。

cues.en: That's an enormous reserve.
cues.zh: 那是非常庞大的储量。

cues.en: But what time is it when the remaining reserve is three times the total of all you've used in all of history? And the answer is two
cues.zh: 但是，当剩余储量是历史总用量的三倍时，现在是几点钟？答案是差两

cues.en: minutes before twelve.
cues.zh: 分钟到十二点。

cues.en: Well, we know for 7%
cues.zh: 我们知道，对于 7% 的

cues.en: growth, the doubling time is ten years. We go from 1981
cues.zh: 增长率，翻倍时间是十年。我们从 1981 年

cues.en: on the 7% curve, the total usage in all history would add up to a thousand billion barrels and be a thousand billion left.
cues.zh: 按照 7% 的曲线，历史总用量将达到一万亿桶，同时还剩下一万亿桶。

cues.en: At that point, the remaining oil would be equal in quantity to the total of all that we had used in something like a hundred and thirty years of the oil industry on this earth. By most measures, you'd say that is an enormous remaining reserve.
cues.zh: 到那时，剩余石油量将等于人类在地球石油工业约 130 年里用掉的总和。按大多数标准来看，这都是一笔巨大的剩余储量。

cues.en: But what time is it
cues.zh: 但是，现在的时刻是几点，

cues.en: when the remaining reserve is
cues.zh: 当剩余储量

cues.en: equal to all that you've used in all of history?
cues.zh: 正好等于有史以来消耗的总量时？

cues.en: And the answer is it's one minute before twelve.
cues.zh: 答案是：差一分钟到十二点。

cues.en: So, go one more decade to the turn of the century. That's like right now.
cues.zh: 再过十年，就到了世纪之交。也就是差不多现在这个时候。

cues.en: That's when 7% would finish using up the oil reserves of the earth.
cues.zh: 按照 7% 的速度，地球上的石油储量就在此时彻底耗尽。

cues.en: Now, let's look at this in a very nice graphical way. Suppose the area of this tiny rectangle represents all the oil we used on this earth before 1940.
cues.zh: 现在，我们用一种非常直观的图表方式来看。假设这个小矩形的面积代表 1940 年之前人类在地球上消耗的所有石油。

cues.en: Then in the decade of the forties, we used this much. That's equal to the total of all that have been used in all of history. In the decade of the fifties, we used this much, that's equal to the total of all that have been used in all of history. In the decade of the sixties, we used this much, and again, that's equal to the total of all the preceding usage. Now, here we see graphically what President Carter told us.
cues.zh: 然后在 40 年代这十年里，我们消耗了这么多。这等于有史以来的总用量。在 50 年代，我们消耗了这么多，同样等于有史以来的总用量。在 60 年代，我们消耗了这么多，又一次等于此前所有历史用量的总和。现在，我们从图形上看到了 Carter 总统告诉我们的内容。

cues.en: Now if that 7%
cues.zh: 如果那个 7% 的增长率

cues.en: had continued through the seventies, eighties and nineties, there is what we need.
cues.zh: 继续贯穿 70、80 和 90 年代，这就是我们所需的总量。

cues.en: But that's all the oil there is.
cues.zh: 但这已经是全部的石油储量了。

cues.en: Now there's a widely held belief that if you throw enough money at holes in the ground, oil is sure to come up.
cues.zh: 现在有一种普遍的看法：只要往地洞里砸足够的钱，石油就一定会冒出来。

cues.en: Well, there will be discoveries in new oil. There may be major discoveries. But look, we have to discover this much new oil if we would have that 7% growth continue ten more years.
cues.zh: 当然，确实会有新石油被发现。也可能会有重大发现。但请注意，要想让 7% 的增长再持续十年，我们必须发现这么多的新石油。

cues.en: Well, ask yourself, what do you think is the chance that oil discovered after the close of our class today will be in an amount equal to the total of all that we've known about in all of history?
cues.zh: 好，问问自己：今天下课后才发现的石油，总量能等于历史上已知全部石油总量的概率有多大？

cues.en: And then realize if all that new oil could be found,
cues.zh: 然后想想，就算这些新石油都能被发现，

cues.en: that would be sufficient to let the historic
cues.zh: 那也足以让历史上的

cues.en: growth continue ten
cues.zh: 增长继续十

cues.en: more
cues.zh: 多

cues.en: years.
cues.zh: 年。

cues.en: What it's interesting to read what the experts say. Here's an interview in Time Magazine
cues.zh: 有意思的是，看看专家怎么说。这是《时代》杂志的一篇采访，

cues.en: with one of the most widely quoted important oil thing experts in all of Texas. They ask him, but haven't many of our bigger fields been drilled nearly dry? He responds saying there's still as much oil to be found in The US as has ever been produced.
cues.zh: 采访对象是得克萨斯州最常被引用、最重要的石油专家之一。他们问他：我们很多大油田难道不是都快钻干了吗？他回答说，美国还能发现的石油，和过去已生产的石油一样多。

cues.en: Now let's assume he's right.
cues.zh: 现在假设他说得对。

cues.en: What time is it?
cues.zh: 现在几点了？

cues.en: And the answer is it's one minute before twelve.
cues.zh: 答案是，离十二点还差一分钟。

cues.en: I've read several things this guy's written. I don't think he has any understanding of this very simple
cues.zh: 我读过这人的一些文章。我觉得他根本不理解这个很简单的

cues.en: arithmetic.
cues.zh: 算术。

cues.en: Well, in the crisis back in the seventies, ads such as this appeared.
cues.zh: 好，在七十年代的那场危机中，出现过这样的广告。

cues.en: This is from the American Electric Power Company. It was a bit reassuring, so they're saying, now don't worry too much because we're sitting on half of the world's known supply of coal,
cues.zh: 这则来自美国电力公司。它有点让人安心，他们说：别太担心，因为我们坐拥世界已知煤炭供应的一半，

cues.en: enough for over five hundred years.
cues.zh: 足够用五百多年。

cues.en: Now, where did that five hundred year figure come from?
cues.zh: 那么，这个五百年的数字从哪来的？

cues.en: Well, it may have had its origin in this report to the Committee on Interior and Insular Affairs of the United States Senate because in that report we find this sentence:
cues.zh: 它可能源自提交给美国参议院内政与岛屿事务委员会的报告，因为报告里有这样一句话：

cues.en: At current levels of output and recovery, these American coal reserves can be expected to last more than five hundred years.
cues.zh: 按当前的产量和采收率，这些美国煤炭储量预计能持续五百多年。

cues.en: There is one of the most dangerous statements in the literature.
cues.zh: 这是文献中最危险的说法之一。

cues.en: It's dangerous because it's true.
cues.zh: 它危险，因为它是真的。

cues.en: But it isn't the truth that makes it dangerous. The danger lies in the fact that people take the sentence apart.
cues.zh: 但让它危险的并不是这个事实。危险在于，人们把这句话拆开来看。

cues.en: They just say coal will last five hundred years.
cues.zh: 他们只说煤炭能用五百年。

cues.en: They forget the caveat with which the sentence started. What were those opening words?
cues.zh: 他们忘了这句话开头的限定条件。开头是哪几个词？

cues.en: At current
cues.zh: 按当前

cues.en: levels. Now, does that mean? It means if and only if we maintain zero growth of coal production in this country. So, let's look at a few numbers. We go to the annual energy review published by the US Department of Energy. They give this figure as the coal demonstrated reserve base and it carries a footnote that says about half the demonstrated reserve base is estimated to be recoverable.
cues.zh: 水平。那这是什么意思？意思是，仅当我们这个国家的煤炭产量保持零增长。来看几个数字。我们查美国能源部发布的《年度能源评论》。他们给出这个数字作为煤炭探明储量基础，并附有脚注：探明储量基础中约一半估计可采收。

cues.en: You cannot recover and use a 100% of the coal that's in the ground.
cues.zh: 你不可能采收并使用地下百分之百的煤。

cues.en: So this number is half of this number, and we'll come back to those in just a moment.
cues.zh: 所以这个数字是这个数字的一半，我们稍后再回来看它们。

cues.en: Now, the report also tells us that in the year 1971,
cues.zh: 报告还告诉我们，1971年，

cues.en: we were mining coal in this country at this rate. Twenty years later, 1991,
cues.zh: 我们国家当时采煤的速度是这样的。二十年后，1991年，

cues.en: we were mining at this rate. Put those numbers together and the average growth rate of coal production in those twenty years was 2.86%
cues.zh: 我们以这样的速度采煤。把这些数字放在一起，那二十年煤炭产量的平均增长率是2.86%

cues.en: per year.
cues.zh: 每年。

cues.en: And so we have to ask, well, how long could a resource last if you had steady growth in the rate of consumption till the last bit of it was used?
cues.zh: 因此我们必须问：如果消耗率持续增长，直到资源的最后一点也被用尽，这种资源还能维持多久？

cues.en: Well, I'll just show you that equation for the expiration
cues.zh: 我来给你们看看那个计算资源

cues.en: time. I'll tell you it takes first year college calculus to derive that equation, so it can't be very difficult.
cues.zh: 有效期的方程。我告诉你们，推导这个方程只需要大学一年级的微积分，所以它不会很难。

cues.en: You know, I have the feeling there must be dozens of people in this country who have had first year college calculus.
cues.zh: 你知道，我觉得这个国家肯定有几十个人学过大学一年级的微积分。

cues.en: But let me suggest I think that equation is probably the best kept scientific secret of the century.
cues.zh: 但我想说，我认为这个方程可能是本世纪保守得最好的科学秘密。

cues.en: Now let me show you why.
cues.zh: 现在让我来说明原因。

cues.en: If you use that equation to calculate the life expectancy
cues.zh: 如果用这个方程计算资源的预期使用年限

cues.en: of the
cues.zh: 对于

cues.en: reserve base or of the one half the reserve base that's estimated to be recoverable
cues.zh: 储量基础，或者估计可采出的储量基础的一半，

cues.en: for different steady rates of growth, you find if the growth rate is zero, that a small estimate would go about two forty years. The large one would go close to five hundred years.
cues.zh: 在不同的稳定增长率下，你会发现，如果增长率为零，较小的估算值大约能维持240年，较大的估算值则接近500年。

cues.en: So that report to the Congress was correct.
cues.zh: 所以，那份提交给国会的报告是正确的。

cues.en: But look what we get when we plug in steady growth.
cues.zh: 但看看我们在代入稳定增长率后得到的结果。

cues.en: Back in the nineteen seventies,
cues.zh: 回到20世纪70年代，

cues.en: we had national goal of achieving 8% per year growth rate in coal production in The United States.
cues.zh: 当时美国制定了煤炭产量每年增长8%的国家目标。

cues.en: If that could be achieved and continued, coal would last between thirty seven and forty six years.
cues.zh: 如果这个目标能够实现并持续下去，煤炭还能维持37到46年。

cues.en: President Carter cut that goal roughly in half, hoping to reach 4% per year. If that could continue, coal would last between fifty nine and seventy five years.
cues.zh: Carter总统将这个目标大致削减了一半，希望达到每年4%的增长率。如果这种增长能够持续，煤炭还能维持59到75年。

cues.en: Here's that 2.86
cues.zh: 这就是我们刚才看到的2.86，

cues.en: that we just saw, the average for a recent twenty year period. If that could continue, coal would run out between seventy two and ninety four years.
cues.zh: 即最近20年期间的平均值。如果这种增长能够持续，煤炭将在72到94年内耗尽。

cues.en: That's within the life expectancy of children born today.
cues.zh: 这就在今天出生的孩子的预期寿命之内。

cues.en: The only way we're going to get anywhere near this widely quoted five hundred year figure
cues.zh: 我们要想接近这个被广泛引用的500年数字，

cues.en: is to do simultaneously
cues.zh: 唯一的办法是同时做到

cues.en: two
cues.zh: 两件

cues.en: highly improbable
cues.zh: 极不可能的

cues.en: things.
cues.zh: 事情。

cues.en: Number one, we've got to figure out how to use a 100%
cues.zh: 第一，我们得想办法利用地下煤炭的

cues.en: of the coal that's in the ground.
cues.zh: 地下的煤炭。

cues.en: Number two,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: we've got to figure out how to have five hundred years of zero growth of coal production.
cues.zh: 我们得想办法让煤炭产量保持500年零增长。

cues.en: Now, are simple facts.
cues.zh: 现在，事实很简单。

cues.en: Just look at those numbers.
cues.zh: 看看这些数字就知道了。

cues.en: I got a report recently
cues.zh: 我最近收到一份报告，

cues.en: from the coal fields of Kentucky,
cues.zh: 来自肯塔基州的煤田、

cues.en: West Virginia, Virginia,
cues.zh: 西弗吉尼亚州和弗吉尼亚州，

cues.en: these giant bituminous
cues.zh: 这些巨大的烟煤

cues.en: coal fields that supply a large fraction of the electricity in the Eastern United States.
cues.zh: 煤田为美国东部大部分地区提供电力。

cues.en: They estimate that maybe they have another thirty years of coal mining before it will become uneconomical
cues.zh: 报告估计，这些地方也许还可以开采煤炭30年，之后采煤就会变得不经济，

cues.en: to mine there. And then what will we do when we want to switch on the lights?
cues.zh: 到那时，如果我们想打开电灯，该怎么办？

cues.en: Let's now go back and note that in the 1970s,
cues.zh: 现在我们回头看看，20世纪70年代，

cues.en: there was great national concern about energy.
cues.zh: 全国曾经非常关注能源问题。

cues.en: But this concern disappeared in the 1980s.
cues.zh: 但这种担忧在20世纪80年代消失了。

cues.en: Now the concerns about energy in the 1970s prompted experts,
cues.zh: 20世纪70年代对能源的担忧促使专家们、

cues.en: journalists and scientists
cues.zh: 记者和科学家们

cues.en: to assure the American people that there was no reason to be concerned. So let's go back now and look at some of those assurances from the seventies
cues.zh: 向美国人民保证，没有理由担心。所以现在让我们回顾一下70年代的一些保证，

cues.en: so we can see what to expect
cues.zh: 这样我们就能看看

cues.en: as the energy crisis returns.
cues.zh: 当能源危机卷土重来时，会发生什么。

cues.en: Here is the director of the Energy Division of the Oak Ridge National Laboratories.
cues.zh: 这里是橡树岭国家实验室能源部门的主任。

cues.en: He's telling us how expensive it is to import oil,
cues.zh: 他在告诉我们进口石油的成本有多高，

cues.en: telling us we must have big increases in our use of coal.
cues.zh: 告诉我们必须大幅增加煤炭的使用。

cues.en: Under these conditions, he estimates America's coal reserves are so huge they could last a minimum of three hundred years, probably a maximum of a thousand years.
cues.zh: 在这种条件下，他估计美国的煤炭储量极其巨大，最少能用三百年，最多可能达到一千年。

cues.en: Now you've just seen the facts.
cues.zh: 刚才你们看到了事实。

cues.en: Now you see what an expert tells us. And what can you conclude?
cues.zh: 现在你们听到一位专家的说法。那你们能得出什么结论？

cues.en: There was a three hour television special on CBS on energy. The reporter said by the lowest estimate,
cues.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）做过一个关于能源的三小时电视专题节目。记者说，按最低估计，

cues.en: we have enough coal for two hundred years, but the highest enough for more than a thousand years.
cues.zh: 我们的煤够用两百年，按最高估计够用一千多年。

cues.en: You've just seen the facts. Now you see what a journalist tells us after careful study.
cues.zh: 刚才你们看到了事实。现在你们听到的是一位记者经过仔细研究后的说法。

cues.en: And what can you conclude?
cues.zh: 那你们能得出什么结论？

cues.en: In the Journal of Chemical Education, on the page for high school chemistry teachers,
cues.zh: 在《化学教育杂志》面向高中化学教师的版面上，

cues.en: an article written by the scientific staff of the journal, we read that our proved coal reserves are enormous and they give a figure. These could satisfy present US energy needs for nearly a thousand years.
cues.zh: 有一篇由期刊科学编辑团队撰写的文章，文中说我们已探明的煤炭储量非常巨大，还给出了一个数字：这些储量能满足美国近一千年的能源需求。

cues.en: Let's do long division. You take the coal they say is there, divide by what was then the current rate of consumption,
cues.zh: 我们来做个除法。把他们说的煤的总量，除以当时的消费速率，

cues.en: and you get a hundred and eighty years.
cues.zh: 得到的是一百八十年。

cues.en: Now they didn't say current rate of consumption. They said present US energy needs.
cues.zh: 他们没说“当前消费速率”，他们说的是“美国当前的能源需求”。

cues.en: Coal today supplies about one fifth, around 20% of the energy that we use in this country. So if you'd like to calculate how long this quantity of coal could satisfy present US energy needs, you have to multiply this denominator by five. When you do that, you get thirty six years. They said nearly a thousand years.
cues.zh: 如今煤炭大约只供应美国所用能源的五分之一，即约20%。所以如果你想计算这些煤能支撑美国当前能源需求多久，就得把分母乘以五。这样一算，得到的是三十六年。而他们说的是将近一千年。

cues.en: Newsweek magazine and a cover story on energy said, at present rates of consumption,
cues.zh: 《新闻周刊》一篇关于能源的封面报道说，按当前的消费速率，

cues.en: we have enough coal for six hundred and sixty six point five years.
cues.zh: 我们的煤够用六百六十六点五年。

cues.en: And the point five means they think it'll run out in July instead of January.
cues.zh: 那个“点五”的意思是，他们觉得煤会在七月而不是一月耗尽。

cues.en: Now, if you round that off and say roughly six hundred years,
cues.zh: 好，如果把这个数取整，说大约六百年，

cues.en: 600 is close enough to 500 to lie within the uncertainty of our knowledge of the size of the resource. So, with that observation,
cues.zh: 六百和五百足够接近，落在我们对资源储量认知的不确定范围之内。所以基于这一点，

cues.en: that is a correct statement. At present rates, meaning zero growth, we have enough coal for around six hundred years.
cues.zh: 这个说法是正确的。按当前速率——也就是零增长——我们的煤够用大约六百年。

cues.en: The whole point of the story that this led into was that we have to have rapid growth in coal consumption in The United States. Now it's obvious, isn't it, if you have the growth they're writing about,
cues.zh: 这个故事引出的核心观点是，美国的煤炭消费必须快速增长。现在很明显了，不是吗？如果按照他们所说的那种增长，

cues.en: it won't last as long as they said it would last with zero growth. They never mentioned this. I wrote them a long letter, told them I thought this was a serious misrepresentation
cues.zh: 煤就不会像他们在零增长假设下说的那样耐用了。他们对此只字未提。我给他们写了一封长信，告诉他们我认为这是一种严重的误导——

cues.en: to give the readers the feeling that we can have all the growth that they're writing about and still have coal around for six
cues.zh: 让读者以为我们既能实现他们鼓吹的那种增长，煤还能再撑六

cues.en: fifty years. I got back a nice, firm letter. It had nothing to do with what I'd tried to explain to them.
cues.zh: 百五十年。我收到了一封客气而强硬的回信，内容却和我试图解释的问题毫无关系。

cues.en: I gave this talk at a high school in Omaha, and after the talk, the high school physics teacher came to me, and he had a booklet. He said, Have you seen this? I hadn't seen it. He said, Look at this.
cues.zh: 我在奥马哈的一所高中做过这个演讲。演讲结束后，那所高中的物理老师拿着一个小册子来找我。他说：你见过这个吗？我没见过。他说：看看这个。

cues.en: We've got coal coming out of our ears.
cues.zh: 我们的煤多得都快从耳朵里冒出来了。

cues.en: As reported by Forbes Magazine, now that's a prominent business magazine,
cues.zh: 据《福布斯》杂志报道——那可是本知名商业杂志——

cues.en: The United States has four thirty seven billion tons of known coal reserves. That is a good figure.
cues.zh: 美国已探明煤炭储量为 4370 亿吨。这个数字很可观。

cues.en: This is equivalent to a lot of BTUs
cues.zh: 这相当于大量 BTU

cues.en: or it's enough energy to keep 100,000,000
cues.zh: 或者说，这些能量足以让 1 亿

cues.en: large electric generating plants going for the next eight hundred years or so. Now the teacher said to me, How can that be true?
cues.zh: 座大型发电厂继续运转大约八百年。然后老师问我：这怎么可能？

cues.en: That's one large electric generating plant for every two people in The United States.
cues.zh: 这相当于美国每两个人就有一座大型发电厂。

cues.en: I said, of course it can't be true. It's absolute nonsense.
cues.zh: 我说，当然不可能。这纯属胡说八道。

cues.en: Let's do long division to see how crazy it is. So you take the coal, they say is there, divide by what was then the current rate of consumption, you find you couldn't keep that rate up for 800.
cues.zh: 咱们做个长除法，看这有多离谱。拿他们说存在的煤，除以当时的消费速度，你会发现根本撑不了 800 年。

cues.en: We hardly have 500
cues.zh: 我们几乎连 500

cues.en: large electric generating plants. They said it would be good for a 100,000,000
cues.zh: 座大型发电厂都没有。他们却说这够 1 亿

cues.en: such plants.
cues.zh: 座这样的发电厂用。

cues.en: Time magazine tells us that beneath the pits heads of Appalachia and the Ohio Valley and under the sprawling strip mines of the West lie coal seams rich enough to meet the country's power needs for centuries
cues.zh: 《时代》杂志告诉我们，在阿巴拉契亚和俄亥俄河谷的矿井口之下，以及西部绵延的露天矿之下，埋藏着丰富的煤层，足以满足这个国家几个世纪的电力需求

cues.en: no matter how much energy consumption may grow.
cues.zh: 无论能源消费增长多少。

cues.en: And so I give you a very fundamental observation.
cues.zh: 所以，我要给大家一个非常基本的观察结论。

cues.en: Don't believe any prediction
cues.zh: 不要相信任何预测

cues.en: of the life expectancy of a nonrenewable
cues.zh: 关于不可再生

cues.en: resource until you have confirmed the prediction by repeating the calculation.
cues.zh: 资源的寿命，除非你重复计算并证实这个预测。

cues.en: As a corollary, we have to note that the more optimistic the prediction, the greater is the probability that it's based on faulty arithmetic
cues.zh: 推论是，我们必须注意：预测越乐观，它基于错误算术

cues.en: or on no arithmetic
cues.zh: 或者根本没有算术

cues.en: at all.
cues.zh: 的可能性就越大。

cues.en: Again from Time Magazine,
cues.zh: 还是《时代》杂志的说法，

cues.en: energy industries agree that to achieve some form of energy self sufficiency, The US must mine all the coal that it can.
cues.zh: 能源行业一致认为，要实现某种形式的能源自给自足，美国必须尽可能多地开采煤炭。

cues.en: Now think about that for just a moment.
cues.zh: 现在稍微想一想这句话。

cues.en: Let me paraphrase it.
cues.zh: 我换个说法。

cues.en: The more rapidly we consume our resources, the more self sufficient we'll be.
cues.zh: 我们消耗资源越快，就越能自给自足。

cues.en: Now isn't that what it says?
cues.zh: 这不就是它说的意思吗？

cues.en: Well, David Brower called this the policy of strength through exhaustion.
cues.zh: David Brower 把这种政策称为“通过耗尽获得力量”。

cues.en: Now here's an example of strength through exhaustion.
cues.zh: 下面就是一个“通过耗尽获得力量”的例子。

cues.en: Here is William Simon, energy advisor to the President of The United States.
cues.zh: 这是 William Simon，美国总统的能源顾问。

cues.en: Simon says we should be trying to get as many holes drilled as possible to get the proven oil reserves. The more rapidly we can get the last of that oil up out of the ground and finish using it,
cues.zh: Simon 说，我们应该尽可能多打井，以获取已探明石油储量。我们能越快把最后那点石油从地下抽出来并用完，

cues.en: the better off we'll be.
cues.zh: 我们就越好。

cues.en: Well, let's look at doctor Hubbard's graph for oil production in the Lower 48 states.
cues.zh: 好，我们来看看 Hubbard 博士关于美国本土 48 州石油产量的图表。

cues.en: There was a long period of approximately
cues.zh: 有一段很长的时期，大约

cues.en: steady growth indicated by this straight line on the semi logarithmic plot.
cues.zh: 是稳定增长，正如半对数图上这条直线所示。

cues.en: But for quite a while now,
cues.zh: 但很长一段时间以来，

cues.en: has fallen below the growth curve while our demand continued on up this growth curve until the nineteen seventies.
cues.zh: 已经跌到增长曲线以下，而我们的需求却沿着这条增长曲线继续上升，直到20世纪70年代。

cues.en: Now, it's obvious the difference between those two curves has to be made up with imports.
cues.zh: 现在，这两条曲线之间的差额显然只能靠进口来弥补了。

cues.en: And it was in early nineteen ninety five
cues.zh: 那是在1995年初。

cues.en: that the news told us that year 1994
cues.zh: 那年1994年，新闻告诉我们

cues.en: was the first year in our nation's history in which we had to import more oil than we were able to get out of our own ground.
cues.zh: 那是我国历史上第一年，我们不得不进口的石油超过从本国土地中开采的石油。

cues.en: Well, maybe you're wondering, does it make any sense to imagine that we could have steady growth in the rate of consumption of a resource till the last bit of it was used and then the rate of consumption would plunge abruptly to zero? I say, no, that does not make sense. You say, alright, why bother us then with the calculation of this expiration time?
cues.zh: 也许你在想，想象一种资源的消耗速率稳步增长，直到最后一点被用完，然后消耗速率突然降到零，这有意义吗？我说，不，这没有意义。你说，那好吧，那为什么还要费心计算这个耗尽时间呢？

cues.en: My answer is this: Every segment of our society, our business leaders, government leaders, political leaders, the local level, state level, national level, everyone aspires
cues.zh: 我的答案是：我们社会的每个群体，商界领袖、政府领袖、政治领袖，地方层面、州层面、国家层面，每个人都渴望

cues.en: to maintain a society in which all measures of material consumption continue to grow steadily
cues.zh: 为了维持一个社会，让物质消费的各项指标持续稳步增长

cues.en: year after year after year, world without end.
cues.zh: 年复一年，永无止境。

cues.en: Now, since that's so central to everything we do,
cues.zh: 既然这对我们所做的一切都如此核心，

cues.en: we ought to know where it would lead.
cues.zh: 我们本该知道这会通向何方。

cues.en: On the other hand, we should recognize there is a better model.
cues.zh: 另一方面，我们得认识到还有更好的模式。

cues.en: We turn again to the work of the late Doctor. Hubbard. He has plotted the rate of consumption of resources that have already expired. He finds, yes, there is an early period of steady growth in the rate of consumption,
cues.zh: 我们再次回到已故的 Hubbard 博士的工作。他绘制了那些已经耗尽的资源的消耗速率曲线。他发现，确实，在早期存在一个消耗速率稳定增长的阶段，

cues.en: but then the rate goes through a maximum and comes back down in a nice symmetric bell shaped curve. And when he fitted this curve to the data on US oil production back in the 1970s,
cues.zh: 但随后这个速率会经过一个最大值，然后沿一条漂亮的对称钟形曲线回落。上世纪七十年代，当他把这条曲线拟合到美国石油产量数据上时，

cues.en: he found that at that point we were right about there. We were one half way through that enormous resource.
cues.zh: 他发现当时我们差不多就在那个位置。那一庞大的资源我们已经消耗了一半。

cues.en: Now, that's roughly what that Texas expert said in the quotation we saw earlier.
cues.zh: 现在，这大体上就是那位德州专家在我们之前看到的那段引文里说的话。

cues.en: Now, let's see what it means.
cues.zh: 现在，我们来看看它是什么意思。

cues.en: It means that from now on, domestic oil production can only go downhill and it's downhill all the rest of the way.
cues.zh: 这意味着，从现在开始，国内石油产量只会一路下滑，而且之后会一直下滑。

cues.en: And it doesn't matter what they say inside the Beltway in Washington, DC.
cues.zh: 无论华盛顿特区政治圈内的人说什么，都没关系。

cues.en: Now it means we could work hard and put some bumps on the downhill side of the curve. You'll see there are bumps on the uphill side.
cues.zh: 现在这意味着我们可以努力一番，在曲线的下坡段制造一些起伏。你会看到上坡段也有一些起伏。

cues.en: The debate is heating up over drilling in the Arctic Wildlife Refuge. I've seen the estimate that they might find 3,200,000,000
cues.zh: 围绕是否在北极国家野生动物保护区进行钻探的争论愈演愈烈。我看到过一种估计，说他们可能会发现32亿】【。

cues.en: barrels of oil up there.
cues.zh: 那上面有几桶石油。
三十二亿

cues.en: is the area of that little tiny square that's less than one year's consumption consumption in The United States.
cues.zh: 就是那个小方块的面积，还不到美国一年的消耗量。

cues.en: Now, let's look at the curve in this way. The area under the entire curve represents
cues.zh: 现在，我们这样来看这条曲线。整条曲线下方的面积代表着

cues.en: the entire resource of U. S. Petroleum before any of it was used. Now, that area has been divided here into three parts. Unshaded on the left, that's the oil we've taken from the ground. We've used it, it's gone.
cues.zh: 这是美国石油在开采之前的全部储量。现在，图中把这个区域分成了三部分。左边未加阴影的部分，是我们已经从地下开采出来的石油。我们已经用掉了，再也没有了。

cues.en: This vertical shaded band, that's the oil we've drilled into. We found it. We're pumping on it today.
cues.zh: 这条竖直的阴影带，就是我们已钻探到的石油。我们找到了它。今天我们正在开采它。

cues.en: Shaded in green on the right is the undiscovered oil. We have very good ways now of estimating how much oil remains undiscovered.
cues.zh: 右侧绿色阴影部分，是未发现的石油。现在我们已经有很好的方法来估算还剩多少未发现石油。

cues.en: This is the undiscovered oil. This is the oil we're looking for in all those places where drilling is going on. This is the oil we've got to find if we're going to make it down the curve on schedule.
cues.zh: 这就是未发现的石油。这就是我们在所有正在进行钻探的地方寻找的石油。如果我们要按计划沿曲线下降，就必须找到这些石油。

cues.en: Now, every once in while someone reminds me that a hundred years ago someone did a calculation
cues.zh: 现在，偶尔会有人提醒我，一百年前有人做过一次计算

cues.en: and predicted that The US would be out of oil perhaps in twenty five years. We obviously were not. The calculation must have been wrong. Therefore, of course, all calculations are wrong.
cues.zh: 并预测美国可能在二十五年内耗尽石油。我们显然没有。那计算肯定错了。因此，当然，所有计算都是错的。

cues.en: Well, now let's understand what they did a hundred years ago.
cues.zh: 好吧，现在我们来理解一下他们一百年前做了什么。

cues.en: This band of discovered oil a hundred years ago was way over in here someplace.
cues.zh: 一百年前，这条已发现石油的带子还在那边某个位置。

cues.en: At that point, they had no idea how much oil was undiscovered.
cues.zh: 当时，他们完全不知道还有多少未发现石油。

cues.en: So, they just took the discovered oil, divided by how rapidly it was then being consumed, come up with 25.
cues.zh: 所以，他们只是拿已发现石油除以当时的消耗速度，得出了 25。

cues.en: Now, it's clear, you have to make a new calculation every time you make a new discovery.
cues.zh: 现在很清楚，每次有新发现，你都得重新计算。

cues.en: We're not asking today how long will the discovered oil last. We're asking about the discovered and the undiscovered. We're now asking about the rest of the oil. And what does the geological survey tell us? Back in 1984,
cues.zh: 我们今天问的不是已发现石油还能持续多久。我们问的是已发现加未发现。我们现在问的是剩下的全部石油。那地质调查告诉了我们什么？早在 1984 年，

cues.en: they said that the estimated supply in The U. S. From undiscovered resources and demonstrated reserves is thirty six years at present rates of production or nineteen years in the absence of imports.
cues.zh: 他们说，美国来自未发现资源和探明储量的估计供应量，按当前产量速度是 36 年，或者在没有进口的情况下是 19 年。

cues.en: Five years later in 1989,
cues.zh: 五年后的 1989 年，

cues.en: that thirty six years is down to thirty two years. The nineteen years is down to sixteen years. So, the numbers are holding together as we march down the right hand side of the Hubbard curve.
cues.zh: 那 36 年降到了 32 年。19 年降到了 16 年。所以，当我们沿着 Hubbard 曲线右侧往下走时，这些数字是对得上的。

cues.en: So maybe you're wondering, well, why didn't somebody tell us this?
cues.zh: 所以也许你在想，为什么没人告诉我们这件事？

cues.en: It was back in 1956,
cues.zh: 那是在 1956 年，

cues.en: Doctor. Hubbard addressed a convention of petroleum geologists and engineers. He told them that his calculations
cues.zh: Hubbard 博士在一次石油地质学家和工程师大会上讲话。他告诉他们，他的计算

cues.en: led him to conclude that the peaks of US oil and gas production that you just saw can be expected to occur between 1966

cues.zh: 你听说过医生诊断出病人患有癌症，然后告诉病人你得了一种“强健的”癌症吗？

cues.en: We had Americans being killed in the Gulf War.
cues.zh: 海湾战争中，有美国人丧生。

cues.en: What's this person worried about? He doesn't care about people. He doesn't care about people being killed.
cues.zh: 这个人担心什么？他不在乎别人。他不在乎有人被杀。

cues.en: All he's worried about is, Oh, the Gulf situation may hurt Colorado's growth.
cues.zh: 他担心的只是，海湾局势可能会拖累科罗拉多州的经济增长。

cues.en: Now, this incredible addiction is not limited to The United States.
cues.zh: 如今，这种惊人的沉迷并不只限于美国。

cues.en: The Wall Street Journal tells us that the Japanese are so accustomed to growth that economists in Tokyo usually speak of a recession as any time the growth rate dips below
cues.zh: 《华尔街日报》告诉我们，日本人太习惯增长了，以至于东京的经济学家通常把增长率跌破……的任何时候都称为衰退。
请提供需要翻译的英文字幕内容（句子之间用单独一行的分隔），我会按照术语参考逐句译成简体中文。

cues.en: per year.
cues.zh: 每年。

cues.en: What do we do?
cues.zh: 我们要做什么呢？

cues.en: In the words of Winston Churchill, sometimes we have to do what is required.
cues.zh: 用 Winston Churchill 的话说，有时候我们必须去做必须做的事。

cues.en: We must educate all of our people to an understanding
cues.zh: 我们必须教育所有人，让他们理解。

cues.en: of the arithmetic and the consequences of growth, especially in terms of populations and in terms of the earth's finite resources.
cues.zh: 包括其算术原理以及增长所带来的后果，尤其是在人口和地球有限资源方面。

cues.en: We must educate people to recognize the fact that growth of populations
cues.zh: 我们必须教育人们认识到人口增长这一事实

cues.en: and growth of rates of consumption of resources cannot be sustained.
cues.zh: 而且，资源消耗率的增长无法持续。

cues.en: Now, the world is full of people who are yakking about sustainability.
cues.zh: 如今，很多人都在大谈可持续发展。

cues.en: Now, some of them are doing serious,
cues.zh: 其中有些人确实在做一些

cues.en: good things like trying to reduce energy consumption and things like this.
cues.zh: 有意义的事，比如努力降低能耗之类的。

cues.en: Some of them are just trying to
cues.zh: 还有些人只是在想办法

cues.en: attack the word sustainability
cues.zh: 把“可持续发展”这个词

cues.en: onto whatever they're doing, whether it's sustainable or not.
cues.zh: 硬套到自己做的事情上，不管那件事是否真的可持续。

cues.en: We've got to understand the first law of sustainability, and it follows directly from what I've just been talking about. The first law of sustainability is this: population growth
cues.zh: 我们必须明白可持续发展的第一定律，它直接源自我刚才所讲的内容。可持续发展的第一定律是：人口增长

cues.en: and or growth in the rates of consumption of resources cannot be sustained.
cues.zh: 和资源消耗率的增长，都无法持续。

cues.en: Now, this follows from the arithmetic
cues.zh: 这可以从我们花时间推导出的

cues.en: of steady growth that we've spent time developing.
cues.zh: 稳步增长的算术规律中得出。

cues.en: So this isn't an opinion. Opinions are debatable. This is fact.
cues.zh: 所以这不是观点。观点可以争论，这是事实。

cues.en: There's nothing here to debate. You cannot sustain population growth. You cannot sustain growth in the rates of consumption of resources.
cues.zh: 这没什么可争论的。人口增长无法持续，资源消耗率的增长也无法持续。

cues.en: And so it's intellectually dishonest to talk about sustainability
cues.zh: 因此，谈论可持续发展却不强调一个显而易见的事实，在思想上是不诚实的：

cues.en: without stressing the obvious fact that stopping population growth is a necessary
cues.zh: 停止人口增长是实现可持续发展所必需的

cues.en: condition for sustainability.
cues.zh: 条件。

cues.en: Now, it's not sufficient. Stopping population growth in itself is not sufficient, but there's no way you can have sustainability if you don't stop population growth.
cues.zh: 当然，这还不够。仅仅停止人口增长并不足以实现可持续发展，但如果不停止人口增长，就不可能实现可持续发展。

cues.en: We need to educate people to see the need to examine carefully the allegations of the technological
cues.zh: 我们需要让人们认识到，必须仔细审视技术乐观主义者的种种说法。

cues.en: optimists who assure us that science and technology will always be able to solve all of our problems of population growth, food, energy and resources.
cues.zh: 他们信誓旦旦地告诉我们，科学和技术总能解决人口增长、粮食、能源和资源方面的所有问题。

cues.en: Now chief among these optimists
cues.zh: 这些乐观主义者中，最主要的人物

cues.en: was the late Doctor. Julian Simon,
cues.zh: 是已故的 Julian Simon 博士，

cues.en: formerly Professor of Economics and Business Administration at the University of Illinois and later at the University of Maryland.
cues.zh: 他曾任伊利诺伊大学经济学与工商管理教授，后来又在马里兰大学任教。

cues.en: With regard to copper, Simon has written that we will never run out of copper because copper can be made from other metals.
cues.zh: 谈到铜，Simon 写道，我们永远不会耗尽铜，因为可以用其他金属制造铜。

cues.en: Well, the letters to the editor jumped all over and told him about chemistry.
cues.zh: 于是，读者纷纷写信批评他，给他上了一课化学。

cues.en: He just brushed it off. He said, Don't worry. If it's ever important, we'll figure out how to make copper out of other metals.
cues.zh: 他却不以为意。他说：“别担心。真到了需要的时候，我们总会想出办法，用其他金属制造铜。”

cues.en: Simon had a book that was published by the Princeton University Press,
cues.zh: Simon 有一本书由 Princeton University Press 出版，

cues.en: and in that book he's writing about oil from many sources including biomass, and he says clearly there's no meaningful limit to this source except for the sun's energy.
cues.zh: 书中他谈到从多种来源获取石油，包括生物质，并明确表示，这种来源没有什么实际的上限，除了太阳能量之外。

cues.en: He goes on to note, But even if our sun were not so vast as it is, there may well be other suns elsewhere.
cues.zh: 他接着指出：“不过，即使我们的太阳没有现在这么巨大，别处也很可能还有其他太阳。”

cues.en: Simon's right.
cues.zh: Simon 说得没错。

cues.en: There
cues.zh: 确实

cues.en: are other suns elsewhere.
cues.zh: 别处还有其他太阳。

cues.en: But now the question is, would you base public policy
cues.zh: 但问题是，你会把公共政策

cues.en: on the belief that if we ever need another sun, we'll figure out how to go get it and haul it back into the solar system?
cues.zh: 建立在这样的想法上吗：如果我们哪天需要另一颗太阳，总能想办法把它弄来，再拖回太阳系？

cues.en: Now don't laugh. For decades before his death, this man was a trusted
cues.zh: 现在别笑。去世前几十年，这个人一直是一位受信任的

cues.en: policy adviser at the very highest levels in Washington, D. C.
cues.zh: 华盛顿特区最高层政策顾问。

cues.en: Here's a quotation from one of his strong supporters.
cues.zh: 下面是他一位坚定支持者的引述。

cues.en: There was a UN report that talked about the possibility of resource collapse because of population growth. And when asked about the report, HUD Secretary Jack Kemp said nonsense.
cues.zh: 有一份联合国报告谈到了人口增长导致资源崩溃的可能性。被问及这份报告时，美国住房与城市发展部部长 Jack Kemp 说这是胡说八道。

cues.en: People are not a drain on the resources of the planet.
cues.zh: 人并不是地球资源的负担。

cues.en: Malcolm Forbes,
cues.zh: Malcolm Forbes，

cues.en: editor in chief of Forbes Magazine,
cues.zh: 《福布斯》杂志主编，

cues.en: tells us in an editorial that CNN recently ran a silly series
cues.zh: 在一篇社论中告诉我们，CNN 最近播出了一个愚蠢的系列节目

cues.en: purporting to show that the world's in mortal danger because there are too many of us. In the poor countries, the many mouths mean poverty and richer countries are wrecking the earth's atmosphere with pollution.
cues.zh: 声称要表明，因为人口太多，世界正面临致命危险。在穷国，众多人口意味着贫困；而富国正用污染破坏地球大气层。

cues.en: It's all
cues.zh: 这全是

cues.en: nonsense.
cues.zh: 胡说八道。

cues.en: Bill Moyers interviewed Isaac Asimov.
cues.zh: Bill Moyers 采访了 Isaac Asimov。

cues.en: He asked Asimov,
cues.zh: 他问 Asimov：

cues.en: what happens to the idea of the dignity of the human species if this population growth continues?
cues.zh: 如果人口继续这样增长，人类物种尊严这一观念会怎样？

cues.en: And Asimov says it'll be completely destroyed.
cues.zh: Asimov 说，它会被彻底摧毁。

cues.en: I like to use what I call my bathroom metaphor.
cues.zh: 我喜欢用我所谓的浴室比喻。

cues.en: If two people live in an apartment and the two bathrooms and both have freedom of the bathroom, you can go to the bathroom anytime you want, stay as long as you want for whatever you need, and everyone believes in freedom of the bathroom, it should be right there in the constitution.
cues.zh: 如果两个人住在一套有两个卫生间的公寓里，两人都有卫生间自由，你可以随时去卫生间，想待多久就待多久，做你需要做的事，而且每个人都相信卫生间自由，这甚至应该写进宪法。

cues.en: But if you have 20 people in the apartment and two bathrooms, then no matter how much every person believes in freedom of the bathroom, there's no such thing.
cues.zh: 但如果公寓里有 20 个人和两个卫生间，那么不管每个人多么相信卫生间自由，这种东西就不存在了。

cues.en: You have to set up times for each person. You have to bang on the door, aren't you through yet? And so on.
cues.zh: 你得给每个人安排时间。你得敲门喊：你还没完吗？诸如此类。

cues.en: Asimov concluded with what I think is one of the most profound observations
cues.zh: Asimov 最后给出了我认为最深刻的观察之一

cues.en: I've seen in years.
cues.zh: 这是我多年来见过的。

cues.en: Asimov says in the same way, democracy
cues.zh: Asimov 说，同样地，民主

cues.en: cannot survive
cues.zh: 无法挺过

cues.en: overpopulation.
cues.zh: 人口过剩。

cues.en: Human dignity cannot survive overpopulation.
cues.zh: 人类尊严无法在人口过剩下存续。

cues.en: Convenience and decency cannot survive overpopulation.
cues.zh: 便利与体面无法在人口过剩下存续。

cues.en: As you put more and more people into the world, the value of life not only declines, it disappears. It doesn't matter if someone dies.
cues.zh: 当你把越来越多的人放进这个世界，生命的价值不仅会下降，还会消失。有人死了也无所谓。

cues.en: The more people there are, the less one individual matters.
cues.zh: 人越多，单个人就越不重要。

cues.en: Now let me give you two examples of this destruction of democracy by population growth.
cues.zh: 现在让我举两个例子，说明人口增长如何摧毁民主。

cues.en: I joined the faculty here in 1950.
cues.zh: 我 1950 年加入这里的教职。

cues.en: At that time, the population of Boulder was about 20,000.
cues.zh: 当时，Boulder 的人口约为 20,000。

cues.en: There were nine members of the City Council. Today, it's approaching 100,000.
cues.zh: 市议会当时有九名成员。今天，人口已接近 100,000。

cues.en: There are nine members of the City Council.
cues.zh: 市议会仍有九名成员。

cues.en: So in a little over fifty years,
cues.zh: 所以，在五十多年里，

cues.en: the number of people per member of the city council has increased by a factor of five. Democracy in Boulder has declined to 20% of what it was fifty years ago.
cues.zh: 每位市议员所代表的人口数变成了原来的五倍。Boulder 的民主已下降到五十年前的 20%。

cues.en: And the second example has to do with the year 2000 national census.
cues.zh: 第二个例子与 2000 年全国人口普查有关。

cues.en: This showed that in the decade of the nineties, The US population increased by about 13%.
cues.zh: 这表明，在20世纪90年代的十年间，美国人口增长了约13%。

cues.en: Now this means every house seat in the House of Representatives
cues.zh: 这意味着，众议院的每个议席

cues.en: now has 13%
cues.zh: 如今平均多了13%

cues.en: more constituents
cues.zh: 选民

cues.en: on the average
cues.zh: 需要代表

cues.en: than they did 10 ago.
cues.zh: 比10年前多了这么多。

cues.en: And in the last one hour, the world population has increased by about 10,000
cues.zh: 而在过去一小时里，全球人口增加了大约1万人

cues.en: people, and the population of The United States in this one hour has increased by about two eighty people.
cues.zh: 美国人口在这一小时内增加了大约280人。

cues.en: And we have to ask:
cues.zh: 我们必须问：

cues.en: Why don't more U. S. Environmentalists
cues.zh: 为什么更多美国环保人士

cues.en: and environmental organizations
cues.zh: 以及环保组织

cues.en: speak out about the problem of population growth here in The United States?
cues.zh: 不站出来谈谈美国人口增长的问题？

cues.en: The simple arithmetic makes it absolutely clear that long term preservation of the environment in The U. S. Is impossible
cues.zh: 简单的算术已经非常清楚地表明，只要美国人口继续增长，美国的环境就不可能得到长期保护

cues.en: in the face of continued U. S. Population growth. But you hear all sorts of political leaders say, Oh, we can have our growth. We'll call it smart growth. And smart growth will save the environment. Well, we need to know about smart growth. Smart growth destroys the environment.
cues.zh: 但你会听到各种各样的政治领导人说：“我们可以继续增长。我们把它称为明智增长。明智增长会拯救环境。”好吧，我们得看看什么是明智增长。明智增长会摧毁环境。

cues.en: Dumb growth destroys the environment.
cues.zh: 愚蠢增长也会摧毁环境。

cues.en: Now, smart growth just destroys the environment with good taste.
cues.zh: 只不过，明智增长是以更优雅的方式摧毁环境。

cues.en: So it's a little like buying a ticket on the Titanic. If you're smart, you go first class.
cues.zh: 这有点像买一张泰坦尼克号的船票。聪明人会买头等舱。

cues.en: If you're dumb, you go steerage, but the result's the same.
cues.zh: 愚蠢的人会坐统舱，但结果都一样。

cues.en: So, central to the things that we must do is to recognize that population growth is the immediate cause of all of our resource and environmental crises.
cues.zh: 所以，我们必须做的事情中，最核心的一点就是认识到，人口增长是所有资源危机和环境危机的直接原因。

cues.en: And of all the crises,
cues.zh: 而在所有这些危机中，

cues.en: I think this one, global warming, looms larger and more threatening than anything in all of human history.
cues.zh: 我认为，全球变暖比人类历史上的任何事情都更加严重，也更加令人担忧。

cues.en: Now, because of our enormous per capita consumption of resources,
cues.zh: 由于我们人均消耗的资源极其庞大，

cues.en: we can say with confidence
cues.zh: 我们可以有把握地说，

cues.en: the world's worst population growth problem is right here in The United States.
cues.zh: 世界上最严重的人口增长问题就在美国。

cues.en: But you hear all sorts of well meaning people pointing to distant underdeveloped nations and saying they're the problem with overpopulation.
cues.zh: 但你会听到各种善意的人把目光投向遥远的发展中国家，说人口过剩的问题出在他们身上。

cues.en: An average person in The United States in a lifetime will consume something like maybe 30 times the amount of resources that will be consumed by a person in a lifetime in an underdeveloped nation.
cues.zh: 一个普通的美国人在一生中消耗的资源，大概是一个发展中国家的人一生所消耗资源的30倍。

cues.en: We are the problem.
cues.zh: 问题出在我们身上。

cues.en: We have the responsibility
cues.zh: 我们负有责任

cues.en: and we have the authority to deal with the problem here as a domestic problem in The United States.
cues.zh: 也有权力把美国这里的问题当作国内问题来解决。

cues.en: And some years ago, speaking here on the campus of the University of Colorado,
cues.zh: 几年前，我曾在科罗拉多大学校园里发表演讲，

cues.en: our United States Senator Tim Wirth said that the best thing we can do to help other countries stop their population growth is for us to set an example and stop our own population growth here in The US.
cues.zh: 当时，美国参议员 Tim Wirth 说，我们能帮助其他国家停止人口增长的最佳方式，就是以身作则，先停止美国自己的人口增长。

cues.en: We have sent representatives
cues.zh: 我们曾派出代表

cues.en: to international conferences to tell the underdeveloped nations, You're the problem. You've got to stop your population growth. And they just laugh and say, Look, you're the problem with all of your high per capita consumption.
cues.zh: 参加国际会议，对发展中国家说：“问题在你们。你们必须停止人口增长。”而他们只是大笑着说：“看看吧，问题在你们，你们的人均资源消耗那么高。”

cues.en: Now, except for the petroleum graphs, the things I tell you are not predictions of the future. I'm only reporting facts and the results of some very simple arithmetic.
cues.zh: 除了石油图表之外，我告诉你们的内容都不是对未来的预测。我只是在陈述事实，以及一些非常简单的算术结果。

cues.en: But I do this with confidence that these facts,
cues.zh: 但我有信心，这些事实、

cues.en: this arithmetic,
cues.zh: 这些算术、

cues.en: and more important, our level of understanding
cues.zh: 更重要的是，我们对它们的理解水平

cues.en: of them will play a major role in shaping our future.
cues.zh: 将在塑造我们的未来中发挥重要作用。

cues.en: Now, don't take what I've said blindly or uncritically because of the rhetoric or for any other reason. Please, you check the facts.
cues.zh: 现在，不要因为我的措辞或其他任何原因，就盲信或不加批判地接受我说的话。请你们去核实事实。

cues.en: Please check my arithmetic.
cues.zh: 请核实我的算术。

cues.en: If you find errors, please let me know.
cues.zh: 如果发现错误，请告诉我。

cues.en: But if you don't find errors,
cues.zh: 但如果你们没有发现错误，

cues.en: then I hope you'll take this very, very seriously.
cues.zh: 那我希望你们非常、非常认真地对待它。

cues.en: You are important people.
cues.zh: 你们是重要的人。

cues.en: You can think.
cues.zh: 你们会思考。

cues.en: And if there was ever a time when the human race needs people who will think, it's right now. It's our responsibility
cues.zh: 如果人类曾有过需要愿思考的人的时刻，那就是现在。这是我们的责任

cues.en: as citizens in a democracy
cues.zh: 作为民主社会中的公民

cues.en: to think.
cues.zh: 去思考。

cues.en: And so to be successful with this experiment of human life on earth,
cues.zh: 因此，要让人类在地球上的这场生命实验取得成功，

cues.en: mathematics,
cues.zh: 数学，

cues.en: we have to remember the message of this cartoon.
cues.zh: 我们必须记住这幅漫画传达的信息。

cues.en: Thinking is very upsetting.
cues.zh: 思考非常令人不安。

cues.en: It tells us things we'd rather not know.
cues.zh: 它会告诉我们一些我们宁愿不知道的事。

cues.en: We should remember the words of Galileo. He said, I do not feel obliged to believe that the same God who has endowed us with sense, reason and intellect has intended us to forego their use.
cues.zh: 我们应当记住 Galileo 的话。他说，我不觉得自己必须相信，那位赐予我们感官、理性和智力的上帝，会打算让我们放弃使用它们。

cues.en: We should remember the words of Aldous He observed that facts do not cease to exist because they're ignored.
cues.zh: 我们应当记住 Aldous 的话。他指出，事实不会因为被忽视就不存在。

cues.en: And we should remember
cues.zh: 我们还应当记住

cues.en: H. L. Mencken's social philosophy.
cues.zh: H. L. Mencken 的社会哲学。

cues.en: He believed that it was of the nature of the human species to reject what is true but unpleasant
cues.zh: 他认为，人类的本性就是拒绝真实但不愉快的东西

cues.en: and to embrace what is obviously false
cues.zh: 而去拥抱明显虚假

cues.en: but comforting.
cues.zh: 却令人安心的东西。

cues.en: And we should remember Eric Severide's
cues.zh: 我们还应当记住 Eric Severide 的

cues.en: law.
cues.zh: 定律。

cues.en: He was a newscaster who made the transition from radio to television back in the 1950s.
cues.zh: 他曾是一名新闻播音员，20世纪50年代从广播转到了电视。

cues.en: He observed that the chief source of problems is solutions.
cues.zh: 他指出，问题的主要来源是解决方案。

cues.en: Now let's just look at an example.
cues.zh: 现在来看一个例子。

cues.en: The Nile River for thousands of years would flood in the spring and the silt that was carried down by the river would be deposited on agricultural lands on the two sides of the river and this renewed the fertility of the land. They had a sustainable agriculture for thousands of years.
cues.zh: 尼罗河几千年来每年春天泛滥，河水带下的泥沙沉积在两岸的农田上，让土地恢复肥力。他们就这样维持了数千年的可持续农业。

cues.en: But now the flood was a sign of a nuisance as you had cities develop along there and the city people didn't like the floods and then the city people needed electricity. So that was the problem. What was the solution? The High Dam At Aswan. So now let's look at the problems caused by the solution.
cues.zh: 但现在，洪水成了麻烦，因为沿岸发展起了城市，城市居民不喜欢洪水，而且城市需要电力。所以那就是问题。解决办法是什么？阿斯旺高坝。现在来看看这个解决方案造成的问题。

cues.en: First of all, all the silt
cues.zh: 首先，所有泥沙

cues.en: is carried down by the river, is deposited in the reservoir behind the dam. So this means the dam has a lifetime, maybe one hundred to two hundred years. It certainly is not very long.
cues.zh: 都被河水带下，沉积在大坝后的水库里。这意味着大坝有寿命，也许一百到两百年。这当然不算很长。

cues.en: So, it'll be filled and then there won't be the storage capacity that it was designed to have.
cues.zh: 所以，水库会被填满，进而失去当初设计时的蓄水能力。

cues.en: The water that's let out from the dam today is very clear water. So, this means all of the erosion patterns downstream have changed. It used to be deposit here, pick up there, and so on. Now it's pretty much just picking up because it starts out from the dam as clear water. Down at the Delta in Alexandria,
cues.zh: 如今从大坝排出的水非常清澈。这意味着下游所有的侵蚀模式都变了。过去是这里沉积、那里冲刷等等。现在基本只剩下冲刷侵蚀了，因为从大坝流出来的都是清水。在亚历山大的三角洲下游，

cues.en: where the Nile enters the Mediterranean Sea,
cues.zh: 也就是尼罗河注入地中海的地方，

cues.en: they're
cues.zh: 水流正在

cues.en: washing away
cues.zh: 冲刷侵蚀

cues.en: agricultural
cues.zh: 农用

cues.en: land because it's no longer being deposited and the river is just washing it out into the Mediterranean.
cues.zh: 土地，因为泥沙不再沉积，河流直接把土地冲入地中海。

cues.en: And it used to be the load of biological nutrients that were brought down in this river all the time supported a major fishery in the Eastern Mediterranean.
cues.zh: 过去，这条河源源不断带下来的生物养分，曾支撑了东地中海的大型渔场。

cues.en: That fishery is in serious decline because the nutrients no longer reach there. And now in order to have their agriculture, they've got to do irrigation. They've got to buy fertilizer. It takes energy to make the fertilizer, and it could easily be that some of the energy to make the fertilizer comes from the dam.
cues.zh: 那个渔场如今严重衰退，因为养分再也无法流到那里。现在为了搞农业，他们不得不进行灌溉，不得不买化肥。生产化肥需要能源，而制造化肥的部分能源很可能正来自这座大坝。

cues.en: And now there are lots of more agricultural workers waiting barefoot in the irrigation ditches and they're subject to a schistomyosis,
cues.zh: 现在有越来越多的农业工人赤脚在灌溉渠里涉水，他们因此容易感染血吸虫病，

cues.en: which is some kind of a parasite that's carried by things in the water that can get through the skin. And if you're barefoot in
cues.zh: 这是一种由水中生物携带、能穿透皮肤的寄生虫。如果你赤脚在

cues.en: the water, why you can get this. Everything went bad because of the solution to the problem. Nobody looked at what the problems would be caused by solution. This is one of the most important things that we need to remember.
cues.zh: 水里，就会染上这种病。一切恶化都源于当初解决问题的方案。没人预见到解决方案本身会引发什么问题。这是我们必须铭记的最重要的一点。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: here's a challenge.
cues.zh: 我来提个挑战。

cues.en: Can you think of any problem
cues.zh: 你能想到有任何问题——

cues.en: on any scale
cues.zh: 无论在何种尺度，

cues.en: from microscopic
cues.zh: 从微观

cues.en: to global
cues.zh: 到全球，

cues.en: whose long term solution
cues.zh: 其长期解决方案

cues.en: is in any demonstrable
cues.zh: 能以任何可被证明的

cues.en: way aided, assisted or advanced by having larger populations
cues.zh: 方式，因人口的增加而得到帮助、支持或推进吗？

cues.en: at the local level, at the state level,
cues.zh: 无论是在地方、在州一级，

cues.en: the national level or globally. Can you think anything that will get better
cues.zh: 国家层面还是全球范围。你能想到有任何事情会变好吗，

cues.en: if we crowd more people into our communities, into our state, into our nation or on this earth? Think about it.
cues.zh: 如果我们把更多的人塞进社区、州、国家或这个地球？想想看。

cues.en: Will anything get better with increased population?
cues.zh: 人口增加会让任何事情变好吗？

cues.en: And I like the words of the late Reverend Martin Luther King, Jr.
cues.zh: 我很喜欢已故的 Martin Luther King, Jr. 牧师说过的一句话。

cues.en: Said, Unlike the plagues of the Dark Ages or contemporary diseases which we do not yet understand,
cues.zh: 他说：“与黑暗时代的瘟疫或我们尚未理解的当代疾病不同，

cues.en: the modern plague of overpopulation
cues.zh: 人口过剩这一现代瘟疫，

cues.en: is soluble
cues.zh: 是完全可以

cues.en: by means we have discovered and with resources we possess.
cues.zh: 用我们已发现的方法和所拥有的资源来解决的。

cues.en: What is lacking is not sufficient knowledge of the solution,
cues.zh: 我们欠缺的并非解决方案的充足知识，

cues.en: but universal consciousness of the gravity of the problem
cues.zh: 而是对问题严重性的普遍认知，

cues.en: and the education of the billions
cues.zh: 以及对数以十亿计

cues.en: who are its victims.
cues.zh: 受害者的教育普及。”

cues.en: And so I hope I've made a reasonable case for my opening statement
cues.zh: 因此，我希望我已经充分论证了我的开篇论断：

cues.en: that I believe the greatest shortcoming of the human race is our inability
cues.zh: 我认为人类最大的缺陷，就是无法

cues.en: to understand this very simple
cues.zh: 理解这个极其简单的

cues.en: arithmetic.
cues.zh: 算术法则。

cues.en: So I thank you very, very much,
cues.zh: 所以，非常感谢大家，

cues.en: and I'd be happy to answer questions.
cues.zh: 我很乐意回答大家的问题。
